And a response to that from MTGuru:

Duplicated: “O’Carolan’s Welcome”

What is the source of this setting? Shouldn’t the key signature here be G Minor (2 flats)? I’ve heard it more commonly played in A Minor. What is the source of the unusual tune title? All the linked recordings have it as (O’)Carolan’s Welcome. Does anyone play this as a mazurka?

# Posted on April 10th 2007 by MTGuru

My answer to MTGuru’s last question ~ “Not anyone in their right mind!”

↳ Posted by Emmanuel Delahaye on August 24th, 2014.

Chords

Lunasa chords this differently. The first strain cadences in F, and the second strains chords are, in order, Am, Am, G, C, Dm, C, G, C, G, F, Am, G, Am, G, Am, G, Am, Em, Am. I expect the posted chords are more authentic, but I love this version. Almost Scots. Sorry I could not put this in score, but I do not know how to do that yet. Thanks for a wonderful site and a wonderfup song.

Re: Carolan’s Welcome

Researcher on early Irish harp music, Simon Chadwick, gives this a 3/10 rating of actually being by Carolan. It appears untitled in the Forde collection dating to the 1840s. I’ve not been able to access the original, so a correct key is a mystery, but if the D# in the first version is right, perhaps that was played by re-tuning one the sister-stings (C) and choosing a key to make that work?

↳ Posted by UncleJack on November 5th, 2025.
